Clean. This head passes the review. A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

I reviewed head 72c8f293d against main cda3d5896. One commit moved since the base of my earlier read: it names the slice error, not the side, when the depth ladder stopped a ring on an unreadable mesh. I read the whole PR diff again, not only the delta.

## What the law does

- The depth ladder finds the part-top level legal for any ring, because nothing stands above it. `picked_law` refuses a picked ring that walks no level under the local part top, while the operation's levels go under it. The refusal fires before any move: nothing is cached, so nothing can post.
- The message names the ring position, the part top, and the fix: the side to set, or the tool containment. The app resolves Auto before generation, so the advice names the side that actually ran.
- New in this head: the ladder records, per ring, the slice error that stopped it (`Ladder::unread`). When the part could not be sectioned under the ring (a self-touching shell), the refusal names that error and the skipped levels, and does not blame the side. `unread_at` replays `legal_at`'s own probe order, so it names the first plane that failed. I checked the replay order and the cache change line by line: for readable meshes the behaviour is byte-identical to before.
- No new panic path. No unwrap or expect in the changed source. The whole-model source keeps `contour_on_bodies`; only the Selection arm gains the law.

| stitch_cross (held red before; now fixed) | 6 pass, 0.05 s |

| area_open (rewritten test) | 11 pass, 0.24 s |
| tilt | 8 pass, 0.16 s |
| blind_floor, real_tip_contour, solid_law | 7, 4, 4 pass |

| clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings | clean |
| merge-tree with main cda3d5896 | no conflict; GitHub reports MERGEABLE, CLEAN |

The legal cases stay legal, green above: Inside and Auto through a hole cut every level; Outside on an outer wall and Outside on a boss stay legal.

## Mutation check

I changed one guard in `picked_law` (`if !asks_below || trims { continue; }` to always continue), so the law never fires. Exactly the five assert-side tests went red: `contour_outside_hole::outside_on_a_picked_hole_wall_is_refused_by_name_at_every_depth`, `contour_outside_hole::inside_on_a_picked_block_top_is_refused_by_name`, `area_open::a_containment_that_puts_the_tool_in_the_part_is_refused_by_name`, `setup_align::unverified_kinds_are_refused_while_verified_picks_generate_aligned`, and `stitch_cross::a_self_touching_single_body_still_stops_at_its_top_level`. The three legal-side tests stayed green. I restored the file, confirmed the worktree clean, and re-ran the four binaries: all green. The pinning tests hold the law.

## Test rewrite review

- `setup_align::unverified_kinds_are_refused_while_verified_picks_generate_aligned` passes now. The repair is right. The old pick was the first horizontal face, the modelled top annulus; flipped over Y it lies at the setup's Z 0, and Outside of its hole ring the centre runs inside solid at Z 16 and Z 12. The refusal is correct in the setup frame. The test now picks the modelled bottom face (the setup's top, where Outside is air) and still asserts a cut below the top. The annulus stays as a control: it generates as modelled and is refused by name once flipped. The Offset2D refusal and the Contour1 assert do not change.
- `stitch_cross::a_self_touching_single_body_still_stops_at_its_top_level` passes now. It keeps the fail-closed fact and asserts the refusal, the skipped level `0.000`, the `non-manifold` cause, and that the side is not blamed. The one-block reference still cuts below the top.
- `area_open` and `tilt`: unchanged since the base I read. The two dropped asserts pinned the silent top-plane pass this change removes. The new asserts cover the same ground. I found no lost coverage.

## Notes (not blocking)

- Behaviour note: a picked ring over an unreadable (self-touching, non-manifold) mesh is now refused with the mesh named. Before this PR the same pick posted a top-plane-only pass with a note. The ring machines nothing below its top, so the refusal fits the law of the issue. The decision file records the choice and the dropped alternative.
- `contour.rs` is now 461 lines (445 on main; +22/-6, 16 net). The 400-line rule: this PR grew a file already over the limit. The decision file records the split as owed separately.
- Nit: the decision file says the PR adds "about 20 lines" to `contour.rs`; the PR body says 15. The true net growth is 16. The statement around the number is true.
- PR #1934 has merged. The overlap I noted before is resolved: this head merges with main cleanly, and the second `contour_on_bodies` call on main is the whole-model arm, which correctly keeps no law.
- I could not run `cargo fmt --check` on this machine (the same os error 206 the body names). I checked with rustfmt directly: main's untouched files differ from default rustfmt in the same way, so the changed files match the file style. No format defect seen.
